dedupe_keys.name: gridpiq grid project impacts quantification web screening tool

description: GridPIQ (Grid Project Impacts Quantification) is a web screening tool that estimates how a grid project, a technology or policy added at one location, affects the wider power system. It is documented by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, and its reference data are published through the DOE Livewire platform with a record by Sarah Newman. The tool combines project context (baseline load, resilience goals, back-up generation, region, dispatch estimation, grid location, line losses and market prices) with technology modules for energy storage, photovoltaics and electric vehicles, and reports emissions, fossil fuel costs, energy and peak power, ramp rates, EV impacts, PV production, revenue and resilience. Dozens of public data sets provide defaults, and users can upload their own data. Early publications used the name Emissions Quantification Tool. Coverage is US regions. It is accessible online as a web tool with public documentation at no cost. Caveats: the documentation stresses transparency and ease of use over precision, no licence is stated, and the Livewire page could not be read as text on the day. Simulation uses are early screening of storage, PV and EV charging projects for planning and resilience. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
